decisive_reasons: They store different things. OAW copies each source note's body into the page verbatim, with ref, ID and date per source (wiki_sync.py:257-324). graphify stores nodes that point at where things are. The 'why' becomes a `rationale` attribute that is used only for scoring search results (serve.py:414-420, 650-716). Query output prints only d['attributes'] (serve.py:1179-1204), get_node prints label, source, type, community and attributes (serve.py:2815-2839), and wiki.py and cli.py never read `rationale`. Replacing the wiki would lose the decision text, which is the one thing OAW says it exists to hold (README.md:66).

The two cannot share a directory, because graphify deletes files. to_wiki removes every *.md it did not write in that run (wiki.py:355-363, 461-466), and graphify's own reflect.py:22-24 warns that files placed there get clobbered. OAW refuses to overwrite manual pages and keeps annotations across rebuilds (wiki_sync.py:431-438). graphify can never own docs/knowledge.

graphify is weakest exactly on OAW's input, Markdown decision notes. Meaning is extracted from documents only by an LLM, with source_location null (extraction-spec.md:80). That pass is told to add `semantically_similar_to` edges and, in deep mode, to be 'aggressive' with INFERRED edges (:45-48). Its confidence scores are documented as collapsing into two values (:71-73). Its cache is deliberately unversioned (cache.py:28-32). LLM edges from an edited document survive a no-LLM update (watch.py:1389-1393, 2363-2378). Rationale fragments are concatenated with no per-fragment source or date (semantic_cleanup.py:324-336), so a superseded decision looks the same as the current one.

Replacing the wiki breaks OAW's hard contracts:
- OAW allows only standard-library runtime dependencies (AGENTS.md:8). graphify needs networkx, numpy, rapidfuzz, pyyaml and 27 tree-sitter entries (pyproject.toml:14-54).
- The release gate and installer depend on wiki_sync (harness_check.py:17,121,178; oaw.py:237,674).
- graphify's skill.md is 49,252 bytes, against OAW's 24,000-byte skill-body limit (skill-catalog-execution.md:76).
- Its always-on rule makes a graph query mandatory before searching (always_on/claude-md.md:6), which contradicts OAW's 'No router' (README.md:78).
- The catalog never replaces a core capability. The order is: borrow the method, else a pack if the capability is missing, else drop (skill-catalog-execution.md:128-137).

graphify does fill real gaps, so do-not-adopt is too strong. OAW has no code map at all. OAW search is an unranked whole-query substring check (context_hub.py:188-213). Spotting a note that 'conflicts with current code' is left to the agent's judgement (oaw-wiki SKILL.md:19-21). graphify's markdown extractor needs no LLM, records L<n> provenance (markdown.py:493-519), and resolves backtick code mentions to EXTRACTED or INFERRED references edges (markdown_resolution.py:1-40). `affected` walks those edges in reverse (affected.py:12-30). That gap belongs to a capability OAW does not have, so it is pack-eligible.

The user's premise is false. graphify uses no embeddings and no vector store (README.md:38). Its matching is case-folded substring plus IDF, with no stemming, no synonyms and no cross-language matching (query.md:22). For OAW's mixed Traditional Chinese and English notes, it will recall less, not more. Its own detector also warns that a corpus under 50,000 words 'may not need a graph' (detect.py:56). OAW wikis are far smaller: OAW's own repo has 5 manual pages and no docs/raw.
fact_checks: CONFIRMED (both advocates): graphify has no embeddings and no vector store (README.md:38). Query matching is case-folded substring plus IDF, with no stemming, synonyms or cross-language matching (skills/claude/references/query.md:22). The user's 'vectorized data map' premise is wrong.

Ambiguous or unresolved mentions are dropped with no warning: 'a guess is not an edge' (markdown_resolution.py:1-40, 230-252).

CONFIRMED: OAW context_hub search is a whole-query substring check, unranked, returning topic names (context_hub.py:188-213). get prints the whole page (240-250). recall searches for one escaped phrase, case-insensitive, with a sha256 snapshot cursor (401-436). The lint fails on a missing source ref, a duplicate source_id, an orphaned or moved source, or a raw note newer than its page (wiki_sync.py:719-721, 770-817).

NEW (neither advocate caught this): AGAINST's integration recipe contradicts itself. `graphify extract --code-only` and `GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=none graphify extract` both empty doc_files ('indexing code only', cli.py:4169-4180, 4264-4277), so the proposed doc-to-code bridge would get zero edges from extract. The no-LLM markdown layer comes only from `graphify update` (watch.py:2346-2357). update skips docs when the build config records code_only=True (watch.py:175-189, 2353), which is written only for --code-only (cli.py:4004-4009). The workable sequence is BACKEND=none extract, without --code-only, then `graphify update .`. This comes from reading the code only; it was not executed.

NEW: graphify's own benchmarks are weak for question answering. LOCOMO QA is 45.3% against supermemory's 49.7%. LongMemEval-S is 76%, 'tied with dense RAG', at n=50 (README.md:131-136). None of them measures decision recall over curated notes. The README also advertises a paid Graphify Cloud (README.md:30). OAW's own evidence is thin too: its experiments used a hand-made corpus (Memory_System_Experiments_Report_2026-04-21.md:149).
to_measure: A pre-registered A/B on a fixture repo. Corpus: about 30-50 docs/raw notes, including decisions that were later superseded, notes that cite code as `path::Symbol`, and a mix of zh-TW and English. Three arms: (A) OAW recall/get only, (B) OAW plus graphify with no LLM, using the update path, (C) graphify alone with its LLM doc pass. Metrics: decision recall@k, accuracy at spotting superseded decisions, citation accuracy (file and line), retrieval tokens consumed, and wall time.

Notes affected by a code change. Script these changes: modify a symbol, rename one, delete one. For each, measure the precision and recall of `graphify affected <Symbol>` and of a stdlib OAW citation lint in finding the notes that cite it. This matters most for rename and delete, where graphify drops the edge silently.

Does the no-LLM doc layer actually appear? In an isolated venv on a throwaway copy, run `GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=none graphify extract .` then `graphify update .`. Count the references edges from docs/raw headings to code nodes. Confirm zero outbound network and zero LLM calls. Check whether duplicate edges from compiled docs/knowledge pages, which copy raw bodies verbatim, help or add noise.

Determinism and diff noise. Rebuild twice and byte-compare graph.json. Check community and label drift with and without graspologic installed. Measure the size of the graph.json diff for a one-line note edit.
Cross-language recall. Run zh-TW queries against English labels, and the reverse, with graphify query (with and without the skill's Step 0 query expansion) and with OAW recall.

Footprint and portability. Measure install size and time for graphifyy with 27 grammar packages on Windows and macOS. Check whether OAW's harness_check stays green when graphify-out/ exists, and whether graphify ever writes outside graphify-out/.
minimal_integration:
Step 0 borrows the method into OAW using only the standard library, so it works without graphify. This follows the catalog's 'absorb method' first rule.
- Add one convention line to templates/docs/raw/_SOURCE_TEMPLATE.md: cite code as a backticked `relative/path.py::Symbol`.
- Add a lint warning to wiki_sync.py (strict mode makes it an error) for each such citation in docs/raw and docs/knowledge:
  - the path must exist inside the repo (use the existing confined_path);
  - for a .py file, use the stdlib ast module to check that a def or class named Symbol exists.
- Add a test in tests/test_wiki_sync.py. Change nothing in harness_check.
- This closes the gap graphify leaves open: graphify drops unresolved citations silently.

Step 1 is an optional external code map. It is documented in Wiki_Sync_Guide.md under 'Optional code map', and is not added to oaw.py, the installer or any profile.
- The user installs a pinned graphifyy in their own venv or pipx.
- Never install graphify's skill, its always-on CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md block or `graphify hook install`.
- Add graphify-out/ to .gitignore.
- Build:
  - run `GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=none graphify extract .`, without --code-only, because --code-only blocks the docs layer;
  - then run `graphify update .`. This adds the no-LLM markdown heading, link and `references` layer for docs/raw.
- Never run `graphify export wiki` into docs/.

Step 2 is how the agent uses it.
- For code navigation, use `graphify query "<terms>"` or `graphify path A B`.
- After changing code, run `graphify affected "<Symbol>"` to list the docs/raw notes that cite it. Then update those notes and run `wiki_sync.py refresh <topic>` and `lint`, following the oaw-wiki skill.
- Decision questions still go to `context_hub.py memory recall`.

Step 3 is the gate. Only after the A/B shows that arm B beats arm A on locating code and finding affected notes, with no regression in decision recall, propose graphify as a non-default OAW pack (skill-catalog-execution.md:133-137). Never put it in the default slot, and never replace wiki_sync.py or context_hub.py.
